claims.claim_text: Wallach treats premature ejaculation as a normal, preventable, and curable issue with basic physical causes — a mental state of high expectation, infrequency of sex, and too much friction — rather than the 'mental block' or 'guilt' the orthodox sexologist invokes. His approach has three parts: be very open and comfortable with each other's bodies (time spent together unclothed, showers, massages, until nakedness is unremarkable); have frequent sex, which requires effort and romance from both partners; and ensure proper lubrication (natural arousal, or a water-soluble gel such as K-Y Jelly, inserting slowly and letting the partner relax). Ginseng (Panax spp.) and herb combinations (Zumbani) are noted as tonifying agents for potency.

claims.claim_text: Electric shock can be fatal, even from 110-volt home outlets (toddlers with bobby pins or keys, appliances falling into the bathtub, electrical repairs without shutting the breakers); electricity kills by disrupting the heart's electrical signals into fibrillation (quivering rather than beating) and paralyzing the breathing muscles. Wallach's treatment is to shut off the source of electricity or break the electrical contact with the patient, then re-establish the basic functions of life with CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) and oxygen — and have someone call 911 for emergency help.

Treatment of electric shock includes shutting

claims.claim_text: Emesis (vomiting) may signal overeating, cancer, excess alcohol, poisoning, food poisoning, food allergies, or infection; in infants, vomiting with lethargy and fever can be an ominous sign of meningitis, and 'coffee-grounds' vomiting (old blood) signals a bleeding ulcer or stomach cancer needing emergency help. Wallach's treatment is to not eat for several hours, suck ice, and drink small amounts of peppermint tea, chicken or beef bouillon, or athletic fluid/electrolyte replacers; for severe stomach irritation, Pepto-Bismol or Kaopectate (preferably liquid) coats the stomach. To induce vomiting after a non-corrosive poisoning, ipecac syrup (1 tablespoon for children, 2 for adults) is given with a large amount of water, repeated in 15 minutes if needed.

Treatment of vomiting can be simply to not eat

chicken or beef bouillon.

claims.claim_text: Enuresis (bedwetting) in children, Wallach argues, is not the 'genetic'/'passive-aggressive'/'antisocial' problem the orthodox pediatrician or psychiatrist describes, but the result of food allergies (sugar, milk) and/or severe reactive hypoglycemia, complicated by calcium/magnesium deficiency — the same picture as hyperactivity. Diagnose with a pulse test and a six-hour glucose tolerance test. His treatment is eliminating the offending foods and eliminating sugar (including sweet grape and apple juices) from bedtime treats, digestive aids (betaine HCl and pancreatic enzymes) at 75-200 mg three times daily 15-20 minutes before meals, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 and 1,000 mg, plus the base-line supplement program and colloidal minerals.

claims.claim_text: Epilepsy (fits, convulsions) is categorized by severity — petite mal (a brief blank stare or dizziness) and grand mal (a spectacular convulsive attack with stiffening, falling, teeth-gnashing, and jerking, which can be fatal if the patient inhales vomit or hits the head). The orthodox drugs (phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone) stop symptomatic convulsions but have dramatic side effects (uncontrolled eye movements, weakness, arthritis and osteoporosis, rashes, anemia, learning disabilities, hyperactivity). Wallach holds that vitamin B-6 alone at 50-100 mg three times daily will frequently 'cure' epilepsy (long-term use can cause some facial/hand numbness and tingling), and that calcium and magnesium at 2,000 and 1,000 mg per day, folic acid at 15-25 mg per day, and vitamin B-12 at 1,000 mcg per day by intramuscular injection can also be curative, along with manganese at 50 mg per day, zinc at 50 mg three times daily, essential fatty acids at 5 gm three times daily, choline at 4 gm per day, taurine at 500 mg three times daily, and dimethyl glycine at 100 mg twice daily.

Wallach's approach is that treatment is specific to the cause, so a blood test for thyroid function, a glaucoma exam, and consideration of a brain or eye (orbital) tumor are indicated.

claims.claim_text: Eye redness (sties, pink eye) can be caused by dust, pollen allergies, bright sunshine, overwork, irritants (cigarette smoke), staying up late, infection, or a foreign body. Herbs for eye washes include eyebright (Euphrasia rostkoviana), fennel (Foeniculum vulgare), German chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla), oak (Quercus robur), pasque flower (Pulsatilla vulgaris), and cornflower (Centaurea cyanus).

His treatment for this form of infertility includes the baseline nutritional supplement; special attention to selenium deficiency in male infertility; betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day before meals; correcting quality protein intake to a minimum of 80 grams a day (he notes the Recommended Dietary Allowance is only 40 grams a day); and essential fatty acids at 5 grams three times a day.

His treatment of fever can include commercial products such as aspirin, acetaminophen (Tylenol), and ibuprofen (Nuprin); ice packs on the forehead; running cool water over the wrists; cool baths; and herbs including feverfew (Chrysanthemum parthenium), meadowsweet (Filipendula ulmaria), sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides), holly (Ilex aquifolium), white willow (Salix alba), mugwort (Artemisia vulgaris), and cinchona bark (Cinchona succirubra). He stresses these are symptomatic treatments — the basic disease process (cold, flu, pneumonia, cancer, etc.) must also be dealt with forthrightly.

His treatment of fingernail problems should include gelatin (diabetic Jello or Knox gelatin) — especially important for anyone who has been vegetarian for any length of time — essential fatty acids at 5 grams three times a day, and betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day before meals.

claims.claim_text: Hiatal hernia is usually a congenital birth defect (not genetic) but can also be caused by crushing the chest or abdomen, as in a car accident; gas, dyspepsia, reflux, and chest pain that mimics a heart attack are common symptoms, and Wallach notes more than 40% of the USA population has asymptomatic hiatal hernia by x-ray survey. Treatment is usually restricted to managing the gas and dyspepsia: small meals, and sleeping with the head of the bed elevated to prevent nighttime esophageal reflux. When there is a large defect in the diaphragm (paraesophageal hiatal hernia), surgical repair is recommended to prevent strangulation of portions of the stomach, intestine, or liver.

claims.claim_text: Hiccoughs are distracting and bothersome but rarely fatal — the result of spasmodic contractions of the diaphragm followed by a sudden closure of the glottis, sometimes started by swallowing hot or irritating substances. Wallach's treatment includes holding your breath (high blood carbon dioxide inhibits hiccoughs), drinking a large glass of water or orange or lemon juice slowly, applying pressure on the closed eyes with the heels of your hands, and applying digital pressure to the phrenic nerves just behind the sternoclavicular joint (where the collarbone joins the sternum).

claims.claim_text: Hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) is, in Wallach's view, almost always caused by food allergies that produce celiac-type intestinal changes and malabsorption of chromium and vanadium, and/or a high intake of purified sugar and refined flour that increases urinary chromium loss by up to 300%; untreated, it frequently develops into diabetes. claims.claim_text: Immune depression (immune exhaustion) is caused by a chronic process — unrelenting stress, chronic allergies, or chronic infections — that exhausts the immune system so it can no longer protect against invaders such as Epstein-Barr virus, candidiasis, food allergies, arthritis, and cancer; 'anergy' is a state of exhaustion so deep that diagnostic skin tests fail to react even with overwhelming disease. Wallach notes that cortisone, prednisone, and chemotherapy themselves cause immune depression. claims.claim_text: Impetigo (ecthyma) is a form of dermatitis in children — blisters filled with straw-colored fluid or pus, or skin ulcers, mainly on the face, arms, and legs. If clumps of bacteria are involved (as in rheumatic fever), antibiotics (penicillin or tetracycline) are required.

claims.claim_text: Jaundice (icterus, yellow eyes) can be caused by blockage of the bile-duct system in the liver (gallstones, tumor, hepatitis) and/or destruction of red blood cells (Rh factor, blood parasites, malaria); diagnosis is critical. Treatment: exposure to ultraviolet light to speed elimination; a liver flush (three days of apple juice, then a cup of olive oil and a cup of lemon juice); vitamin C to bowel tolerance; vitamin A at 300,000 international units per day as beta carotene; selenium at 500-1,000 micrograms per day; vitamin E at 800-1,200 international units per day; and herbs licorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra), agrimony (Agrimonia eupatoria), celandine (Chelidonium majus), and chionanthus (Chionanthus virginica).

Prevention and treatment: frequent feeding of the infant to reduce absorption of bile pigments, and exposure to blue and ultraviolet light to photo-oxidize the bilirubin (a transient lactose intolerance can accompany light therapy in infants, causing diarrhea, but this does not appear to have any permanent consequences).

claims.claim_text: Ketoacidosis (ketosis) results from a low glucose supply to the liver, which forces it to metabolize fat — producing 'ketone bodies' (acetoacetic acid, beta-hydroxybutyric acid, and acetone). It occurs in diabetes, alcoholism, hypoglycemia, and starvation. Signs include acetone-smelling breath, nausea and vomiting, air hunger, confusion or coma, extreme thirst, and weight loss; a positive urine 'dipstick' for ketone bodies confirms it. Treatment: resolve the basic disease process (diabetes, hypoglycemia, alcoholism, starvation), increase complex-carbohydrate intake, chromium at 50-200 micrograms three times daily, and the baseline nutritional program.

Chelation helps; an acute stone blockage may require morphine for pain and prednisone for three days to reduce ureter inflammation, and a 'lithotripter' (ultrasound) can shatter stones without surgery.

It can result from a blow to the head (good chance of recovery) or from chronic alcoholism and vitamin B-1 deficiency (harder to treat). Wallach notes the same thing happens to unschooled dieters, cancer patients, vegans, and fruitarians who take in less than optimal amounts of complete protein. Treatment: adequate complete animal protein (greater than 120 grams per day), a calorie intake of 3,000 calories per day, selenium at 200 micrograms per day, and chromium at 50-200 micrograms three times daily, plus the baseline nutritional supplementation.

Wallach also states his opinion that home births are safer than hospital births, and notes the hospital caesarian-section rate of 35%, observing that vaginal births earn the obstetrician about $800-$1,200 while caesarian sections earn about $2,500 — his editorial commentary on cost incentives, not a medical claim.

claims.claim_text: Lactase deficiency (cow's-milk sensitivity) is a carbohydrate intolerance caused by a deficiency of lactase, the enzyme needed to break milk sugar (lactose) into glucose and galactose; it is marked by bloating, diarrhea, and violent abdominal cramps after consuming cow's milk and cow's-milk products. Wallach cites prevalences of about 20% in adults of Northwest European origin, 75% in adults of all other ethnic groups, 90% of Orientals, and 75% of Blacks and American Indians, with the ability to digest lactose gradually lost between ages 10 and 20. Treatment: avoid lactose-containing foods and/or predigest the lactose by adding lactase enzyme to milk-containing foods.

Viral laryngitis may be treated with Isoprinosine at 500-1,500 milligrams per day or Ribavirin at 250-1,500 milligrams per day (pregnant women should avoid these drugs — they are teratogenic in lab animals).

claims.claim_text: Legionnaires' disease is caused by infection with Legionella pneumophila; it is characterized by pneumonia, high fever, slow heart rate, dry cough, chills, pleuritis, and diarrhea. A relatively new disease (discovered in 1976), it is fatal in 80% of untreated cases and is diagnosed by growing the organism on charcoal-yeast extract from sputum; immunosuppressed patients (those on chemotherapy, transplant patients, AIDS patients) are most susceptible. Treatment is specific: erythromycin at 500 milligrams to 1 gram orally or intravenously every 6 hours for three weeks.

claims.claim_text: Leptospirosis (Weil's disease, infectious jaundice) is an infectious disease caused by Leptospira, a spirochete bacterium carried by dogs, rats, and various wild animals; people are infected through urine-contaminated water or cuts while skinning or butchering infected animals. Symptoms include anemia, jaundice, proteinuria, hematuria, and occasionally aseptic meningitis, with fever and chills consistent; diagnosis needs blood tests or urine cultures. Treatment with antibiotics is most effective if started within four days of onset — tetracycline at 500 milligrams four times daily is effective.

claims.claim_text: Leukemia (blood cancer) is a cancer of the blood-forming tissues of the bone marrow; no exact cause is proven, though viruses, radiation, and chemicals such as benzene are implicated. It produces a defect in white-blood-cell maturation, flooding the circulation with immature white cells; diagnosis comes from a blood test showing anemia, low platelets, increased lymphoblasts, and an elevated total white-cell count, and symptoms include weakness, joint pain, anemia, enlarged lymph nodes, and an enlarged spleen. Wallach's treatment includes Laetrile, hydrogen peroxide, intravenous dimethyl sulfoxide (said to mature the immature cells), Onco-Tox, shark liver extract, hydrazine sulfate, cesium chloride, polyerga, germanium, carbamide, and as needed micro-dose chemotherapy, intravenous amino acids, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, selenium at 500-1,000 micrograms per day, and vitamin A at 300,000 international units as beta carotene. Specific diagnosis requires culture and/or microscopy of the discharge. Treatment targets the causative organism: vaginal triple-sulfonamide creams, oxytetracycline vaginal suppositories, vinegar douches (30 milliliters per pint of water), and 1.5% hydrogen peroxide (as Oxy-Toddy); gonorrhea also requires systemic antibiotics. Wallach notes that any venereal disease must be reported to the Public Health Department.

He says home water-filtration systems, air filters and conditioners, and the baseline nutrition program can each add years, and that digestive aids (betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes) add another ten — about twenty added years when pursued actively. He attributes the Hunza secret of longevity (averaging 100 years, up to 140) to the daily consumption of plant-derived colloidal minerals, and warns that exercise alone — without attention to food allergies, digestive aids, the baseline program, colloidal minerals, and avoiding pollutants — will only shorten life. He also notes that 40% of hospital patients are there because of iatrogenic (doctor-caused) disease. (Captured for the search corpus as Wallach's general longevity guidance.)

claims.claim_text: For lockjaw (tetanus) — caused by the toxin of Clostridium tetani, a normal inhabitant of animal manure that enters through puncture wounds and paralyzes the voluntary muscles including the jaw (masseter) muscles — Wallach stresses prevention as the best option: make the puncture wound bleed by squeezing it, open small foot or hand punctures to clean with soap and water, then disinfect with 3% hydrogen peroxide, and take cramp bark tea (Viburnum opulus) in tablespoon doses as needed; he says these minimal steps prevent lockjaw almost 100% of the time. Once it develops, treatment requires tetanus-neutralizing (non-fixed) antitoxin, cleaning and disinfecting the infected wound with hydrogen peroxide, penicillin at two million units intravenously every 6 hours OR tetracycline at 500 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours, sedation to control muscle spasms, and intravenous fluids and electrolytes until the patient can eat and drink on their own.

His treatment is: avoid offending food allergens and rotate non-allergic foods; autoimmune urine therapy; chelation with total nutrition for 15-25 infusions; essential fatty acids (salmon oil and flaxseed oil) at 5 grams three times a day; selenium at 500-1,000 micrograms per day; carnitine (printed 'B-carnitine') at 500 milligrams per day; avoid beef, dairy and alfalfa; and daily doses of plant-derived colloidal minerals.

It occurs most in children who play in grass or deep woods or who have a dog that brings home the Ixodes dammini tick, clusters along the U.S. northeastern coast and in Wisconsin, California and Oregon, and is often misdiagnosed as rheumatoid arthritis. His treatment is tetracycline at 250-500 milligrams four times a day for 20 days; in children, whose teeth tetracyclines discolor, penicillin at 20 million units per day intravenously in divided doses.

claims.claim_text: Wallach defines malnutrition as occurring either as an overt nutritional deficiency, secondary to extended use of medications that interfere with nutrient absorption, or as malabsorption from celiac disease or low stomach acid (hypochlorhydria). He argues conventional doctors think of malnutrition only as protein/calorie deprivation and miss macro- and micro-nutrient deficiencies (singly or in combination, especially early), and miss that celiac changes in the small-intestine lining arise from subclinical allergies to wheat, cow's-milk albumen and soy (and rye, barley, beef, eggs). In his framework many degenerative diseases are really malabsorption: diabetes and hypoglycemia as chromium/vanadium deficiencies, cystic fibrosis as a selenium and essential-fatty-acid deficiency, arthritis as a calcium deficiency worsened by excess dietary phosphorus, and cancer as a depleted immune system run out of repair nutrients. He concludes malnutrition from malabsorption is the common denominator of almost all degenerative disease, and that liquid plant-derived colloidal minerals are the most efficient way to get minerals into malnourished people. claims.claim_text: Measles (rubeola) is a highly contagious viral disease of sudden onset with cough, nasal drainage, conjunctivitis, Koplik's spots (eruptions on the mouth and lip lining), and a pimple-like rash starting on the head and neck and spreading to the body, arms and legs; fever to 104°F is common, and pneumonia and encephalitis are unusual but potentially fatal complications. Wallach notes it now affects mainly teenagers and young adults, incubates 7-14 days (the diagnostic Koplik's spots appear about four days after the fever), and that having had measles confers lifelong immunity. His treatment is topical over-the-counter anti-itch products (for example Caladryl) plus herbs: salves of marigold (Calendula officinalis), and taken orally columbine (Aquilegia vulgaris), yarrow (Achillea millefolium) and pleurisy root (Asclepias tuberosa).

claims.claim_text: German measles (rubella, three-day measles) is a contagious viral disease that causes mild symptoms in children, including swollen lymph nodes of the head and neck; its incubation is 14-21 days and overt symptoms may be absent in teenagers and adults. The typical rash appears first on the face and spreads quickly to the body and limbs with a general flush like scarlet fever; adults may have enlarged head and neck lymph nodes and adult males may have brief testicular pain. Wallach's treatment is the same symptomatic therapy used for ordinary (nine-day) measles. He states emphatically (in capitals) that rubella is a dangerous disease in pregnant women that can induce spontaneous abortions and birth defects, and gives his editorial opinion that rubella vaccines will cause similar birth defects and so should be avoided during pregnancy.

claims.claim_text: Melasma (chloasma, the "mask of pregnancy") is dark brown spots with distinct margins on the face and forehead of pregnant women and women on birth-control hormones; sunlight darkens the pigment and the spots may fade after childbirth. Wallach says susceptible people should use sunscreens while in the sun, and notes the spots are cosmetic in nature and appear to be of no consequence to health.
claims.verbatim:

hormones, sunlight darkens the pigment. The
spots may fade after childbirth. Susceptible
individuals should use sunscreens while exposed to the sun

claims.claim_text: For memory loss (senile dementia, Korsakoff's syndrome, Alzheimer's disease) Wallach says there are many causes that should each be looked up separately, including food allergies and hypoglycemia; he advises the pulse test for food allergies/sensitivities and a six-hour glucose tolerance test to rule hypoglycemia in or out. His treatment is: avoid offending food allergens, sugar and alcohol; chromium at 25-200 micrograms three times a day; selenium at 200-1,000 micrograms per day; vitamin E at 800-1,200 international units per day; B-complex at 50 milligrams three times a day; Diapid (vasopressin) nasal spray at 12-16 units per day; Lucidril (centrophenoxine) at 4.4-8.0 grams per day; Dinagen (piracetam) at 1.6-4.8 grams per day (take choline with it); and hydergine at 9-20 milligrams per day.

claims.claim_text: Wallach describes menarche/menstruation: the regular monthly cycle alternating ovulation (mid-cycle, about day 14) with the 3-7 day 'period' (discharge of blood and uterine lining). He notes periods often stop in athletes and women who drop below 20% body fat — of no health consequence in itself, but a signal of being too thin for normal cycling and ovulation. Painful periods (which he usually attributes to essential-fatty-acid deficiency) can be severe enough to force bed rest. His treatment for painful or excessive ('heavy flow') menses: over-the-counter products (for example Midol) and/or herbs — snapdragon (Linaria vulgaris), bethroot (Trillium erectum), black cohosh (Cimicifuga racemosa), blue cohosh (Caulophyllum thalictroides), tamarac (Larix americana), ragwort (Senecio fuchsii), lady's mantle (Alchemilla vulgaris), St. John's wort (Hypericum perforatum), shepherd's purse (Capsella bursa-pastoris), white deadnettle (Lamium album) and yarrow (Achillea millefolium); plus essential fatty acids (salmon oil and flaxseed oil) at 5 grams three times a day, vitamin E at 800-1,200 international units per day, selenium at 500-1,000 micrograms per day, and iron at 25-50 milligrams per day (especially for vegetarian women who don't eat red meat or liver regularly).
claims.verbatim:
essential fatty acids (salmon oil and flaxseed oil) at 5 gm t.i.d.,
vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU/day, selenium at
500-1,000 mcg per day, iron at 25-50 mg per
day

claims.claim_text: Meningitis (infection of the covering of the brain and spinal cord) can be caused by many organisms — bacteria (Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae, Streptococcus/Diplococcus pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes), fungi, and hundreds of viruses. Wallach stresses it is especially dangerous because infants often show only fever and lethargy, and the blood-brain barrier keeps most medications out of the meninges and brain. Symptoms vary but usually include sore throat, fever, headache, stiff neck and vomiting, and children and adults can become critically ill within 6-24 hours of the first symptoms. He warns emphatically that this is NOT a self-help disease: if you suspect meningitis, get the patient to an emergency room immediately and demand help, because patients often die after waiting hours in a waiting room. Treatment requires rapid diagnosis (spinal tap) and injection of antibiotics into the subdural space (under the meninges), total intravenous fluid and electrolyte support, and frequently mechanical respirators.
claims.verbatim:
If you suspect meningitis, this is
one disease that requires rapid diagnosis and
treatment GET PATIENT TO AN EMERGENCY
ROOMSTAT!!! DEMAND IMMEDIATE HELP!!!
Meningitis patients often die because they
have waited 2-4 hours in an emergency waiting room

claims.claim_text: Meningocele (severe anencephaly or spina bifida) is a severe birth defect in which the brain or spinal cord and its coverings (meninges) are exposed because the vertebrae form improperly. Wallach attributes it to a deficiency of folic acid, vitamin B-12, or zinc and vitamin A during early pregnancy — deficiencies that may stem from a poor diet and/or malabsorption in the mother. Severe cases may be debilitating or fatal. Treatment is limited to surgery, so he emphasizes that prevention — correcting these deficiencies before and during early pregnancy — is the goal.
claims.verbatim:
MENINGOCELE (severe anencephlia or
spina bifida): is a severe birth defect that
results in exposure of the brain or spinal cord
and its coverings (meninges) because of improper formation of the vertebrae. This birth
defect is caused by a deficiency of folic acid, B-
12, or zinc and vitamin A during early pregnancy

claims.claim_text: Menkes kinky hair syndrome is considered a genetic disease by conventional pediatricians, but Wallach argues it is a copper-deficiency malabsorption problem of early infancy (for example from celiac disease); he cites the veterinary parallel that copper deficiency causes 'kinky wool' disease. Features include retarded growth, anemia, progressive brain degeneration, sparse brittle hair, loss of hair color, arterial aneurysms and scurvy-like bone disease; hair analysis shows very low copper, and blood shows low copper and low ceruloplasmin. His treatment addresses the malabsorption (avoid wheat, cow's milk and soy) and gives copper intravenously at 200 micrograms per kilogram per day, then copper orally at 1-2 milligrams per day after symptoms improve.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of Menke's syndrome includes dealing with the malabsorption problems (i.e.,
avoid wheat, cow's milk and soy) give copper
IV at 200 ug/kg/day, give copper orally at 1-2
mg per day after relief of symptoms

claims.claim_text: Mercury poisoning can result from ingesting or inhaling any mercurial compound and from off-gassing of mercury vapor from mercury-amalgam dental fillings. Symptoms include gastroenteritis, salivation, burning mouth pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, colitis, kidney disease, gingivitis, mental and emotional disturbances and nerve deficits; Wallach notes many dentists and alternative practitioners think multiple sclerosis may result from mercury poisoning, and that the mental/emotional effects in Victorian 'hatters' gave rise to 'as mad as a hatter.' Diagnosis is easy via hair analysis plus a history of a mercury source. His treatment: remove the mercury source (including mercury-amalgam fillings), chelation with calcium-EDTA (with complete intravenous nutrition), and sweating (sauna), since mercury is excreted in sweat; he adds that selenium-containing colloidal minerals are very effective at removing mercury from the tissues.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of mercury poisoning includes the
removal of the source of mercury including
removing mercury amalgam dental fillings,
chelation with CaEDTA (to include complete
IV nutrition) and sweating (sauna) as mercury
is excreted in sweat.
The use of selenium containing colloidal minerals is very effective in removing mercury
from the tissues

(Captured for the search corpus as a general definition of his therapeutic approach.)

herbs, homeopathy, acupuncture, manipulation and hydrotherapy

claims.claim_text: Methadone is the drug used to ease opiate withdrawal, classically given in just enough amount (usually 20 mg/day) to prevent the most severe withdrawal symptoms; Wallach notes opiate (opium, morphine, etc.) withdrawal is self-limiting and not life-threatening (though addicts in withdrawal often feel otherwise). He recommends doubling the baseline nutrition program for 30 days to help the patient through withdrawal, then dropping to the baseline supplement program and staying on it; do the pulse test for food sensitivities/allergies and a six-hour glucose tolerance test, since people addicted to drugs and/or alcohol frequently have 'addictive allergies' to food and sugar.
claims.verbatim:
The use of double the base line nutrition program for 30 days will enhance the
patient's ability to get through the withdrawal
- after 30 days drop to the base line nutritional
supplement program and remain on it

claims.claim_text: Migraine headaches are often heralded by flashes of light and tingling, occur between ages 10-30, and are more common in women; symptoms include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, digital cyanosis (blue fingers from poor circulation/oxygen), irritability and photophobia (light sensitivity). Wallach rejects the conventional blood-vessel theory, holding that migraines result from food allergies — the 'target' tissue being the arteries (the elastic arteries in the brain constrict while the muscular scalp arteries dilate); use the pulse test to identify the offending foods. Treatment and prevention: avoid the identified food allergens, rotation diets, autoimmune urine therapy, betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 mg three times a day, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, bioflavonoids at 200 mg twice a day, and the baseline nutrition program.
claims.verbatim:

claims.claim_text: Miscarriage (spontaneous abortion) is usually due to deficiencies of vitamins, trace minerals and/or protein — in particular vitamin A, zinc, folic acid, selenium and complete proteins, all essential to maintaining pregnancy. Wallach attributes the underlying malnutrition to restricted diets (weight-loss, incomplete vegetarian or rotation diets) and malabsorption syndromes (such as celiac-type intestinal injury) in the mother, and says these cause both miscarriages and birth defects; use the pulse test to identify offending food allergens. Treatment and prevention: the baseline nutrition program for six months before attempting conception, plus herbs cramp bark (Viburnum opulus), blue cohosh (Caulophyllum thalictroides) and alfalfa.
claims.verbatim:
MISCARRIAGE (spontaneous abortion):
is usually due to deficiencies of vitamins, trace

claims.claim_text: Mitral valve prolapse is a common, progressive change in the left atrioventricular (mitral) valve and the surrounding heart tissue. Most people have no symptoms; some have non-anginal chest pain, palpitations, fatigue and/or breathing problems, and a late systolic heart murmur is sometimes heard during squatting exercises. If you have no symptoms, your activities need not be restricted. Wallach's treatment is selenium at 500 to 1,000 micrograms a day, magnesium at 1,000 milligrams three times a day, salmon oil (a source of omega-3 essential fatty acids) at 1 to 5 grams three times a day and the herb hawthorne (Crataegus oxyacantha), in addition to the baseline nutritional supplement program. He says you can expect significant improvement in 30 to 60 days.

claims.claim_text: Monckeberg's arteriosclerosis is a circular calcification of the media — the middle muscular/elastic layer — of the small arteries. Wallach says this disease is caused by excess vitamin D (hypervitaminosis D), and its symptoms include high blood pressure (hypertension) and angina. His treatment is EDTA chelation, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, selenium at 500 to 1,000 micrograms a day and the baseline nutritional supplement program.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of Monkeberg's arterio sclerosis
should include EDTA chelation, vitamin C to
bowel tolerance, selenium at 500-1,000 mcg
per day and the base line nutritional supplement program

claims.claim_text: Mongolism (Down's syndrome) is a birth defect that Wallach attributes to a zinc deficiency in the earliest moments of conception (he notes one third of the extra chromosome comes from the father). Orthodox doctors instead view it as a chromosomal defect whose risk rises with the mother's age. Newborns are 'floppy', lacking muscle tone; physical and mental maturation is delayed (average intelligence quotient, or IQ, around 50), with a small domed-forehead head, a flattened nose bridge, slanted eyes with epicanthal folds, and Brushfield's spots around the iris. Prevention: follow the baseline nutritional supplement program for 90 days before attempting conception and use the pulse test to find and eliminate the food allergies that block zinc absorption. Treatment: zinc at 50 milligrams three times a day plus the baseline program, again using the pulse test to identify and avoid offending foods. Wallach says you can expect the intelligence quotient to rise by 15 to 20 points and physical features to improve as long as the program is followed; stopping it loses all the gains.

MONGOLISM (Down's syndrome): is a
birth defect caused by a zinc deficiency in the
earliest moments of conception (one third of
the extra chromosome comes from the paternal parent

Wallach says eating a complex-carbohydrate or protein snack on awakening relieves much of the nausea. He also suggests herbal teas of dogwood (Cornus sericea) and mint (Mentha sativa); vitamin B-6 together with a B-complex at 25 milligrams three times a day; essential fatty acids (omega-3) at 1,000 milligrams three times a day; and the baseline nutritional supplement program.

claims.claim_text: Mosquitoes can be kept out of the home with screen windows and doors and electric 'zapper' lights placed 15-25 yards from the back door (the violet light draws mosquitoes away from the house). Wallach notes mosquitoes carry serious human diseases — meningitis and encephalitis in North America; malaria, yellow fever, meningitis and encephalitis in South America. Beyond over-the-counter flying-insect sprays, he says the herb pennyroyal (Mentha pulegium) oil rubbed on the skin and vitamin B-1 (thiamine) at 500 milligrams a day will also help repel mosquitoes.

There are numerous OTC flying

claims.claim_text: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a progressive disease of the central nervous system marked by scattered zones of demyelination (loss of the fatty insulating layer on nerves). Symptoms start between ages 20 and 40 — usually tingling or numbness in the arms or legs (a 'stocking and glove' pattern) — and progress to weakness, clumsiness, visual and balance problems, dizziness and bladder-control trouble; intention tremor, nystagmus and 'scanning' speech form Charcot's triad. Wallach links MS to mercury (he cross-references mercury poisoning) and to the loss of cholesterol-rich myelin. He criticizes the orthodox cortisone/prednisone approach and instead recommends: avoid animal fats; a high intake of fish oil (cod liver or salmon oil) at 5 grams three times a day and flaxseed oil at one tablespoon twice a day (said to raise survival by 50 percent); removal of mercury (amalgam) fillings; calcium 2-aminoethylphosphate (CaEAP) one dose four times a day; octacosanol two capsules three times a day; daily snake-venom injections; D-phenylalanine at 500 milligrams three times a day; betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day; avoidance of known food allergens with rotation diets; and avoiding vitamin C supplements (using green vegetables and juices as a natural source instead). Wallach says the same regimen has also worked for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, or Lou Gehrig's disease).

claims.claim_text: Mumps is a contagious viral disease that causes painful enlargement of the salivary glands, especially the parotids; the virus is highly aggressive and is present in saliva up to six days before illness is felt. Symptoms include fever (up to 104°F), chills, and tender, shiny, swollen skin over the salivary glands in front of and below the ear. In about 20 percent of adult males it causes a painful testicular infection, and testicular atrophy may follow (though hormone production and fertility are rarely affected). Wallach's treatment is symptomatic: pain relief (codeine, acetaminophen/Tylenol, aspirin), bed rest, a liquid diet (chicken rice soup, sugarless Jello, Gatorade, juices) and the herb mullein (Verbascum thapsus) for symptom relief.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of mumps is symptomatic including pain relief (i.e., codeine, tylenol, aspirin,
etc.), bed rest, liquid diet including chicken
rice soup, sugarless Jello, Gatorade, juices and
herbs for symptomatic treatment including
mullein (Verbascum thapsus

claims.claim_text: Muscular dystrophy (MD) is, in Wallach's view, a preventable selenium-deficiency disease — he points out it has been eliminated in livestock ('white muscle disease') by giving selenium to pregnant females and fast-growing young animals. Adequate selenium in preconception women maintains pregnancy and prevents all forms of MD (Duchenne, Erb, Leyden-Moebius, Landouzy-Dejerine, Becker's and Gowers), and he adds Keshan disease (a selenium-deficiency heart-muscle dystrophy) to the list. Food-allergy-driven celiac-type changes in the small intestine are a common cause of the tissue selenium deficiency, so do a pulse test. He says giving selenium and vitamin E by intramuscular or intravenous injection at the very first symptoms can arrest or cure the disease. Treatment of MD and/or Keshan disease: selenium orally (as plant-derived colloidal minerals), intravenously or intramuscularly at 50-1,000 micrograms a day (by weight); vitamin E intramuscularly at 80 milligrams a day; selenium orally at 250-1,000 micrograms a day; vitamin E 800-1,200 (orally); sulfur amino acids (a complete amino-acid infusion intravenously, plus free amino acids orally) and sugarless Jello; essential fatty acids at 5 grams three times a day; avoid food allergens; keep fat under 20 percent of daily calories; choline as soy lecithin at 10-20 grams a day; and avoid exercise for the first month of treatment to protect compromised muscle.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of MD and/or Keshan disease includes the use of selenium orally (plant derived colloidal minerals), IV or IM at 50-1,000
mcg per day (based on weight), vitamin E IM
at 80 mg per day, selenium orally at 250-1 ,000
mcg per day, vitamin E 800-1, 200 orally

claims.claim_text: Muscle cramps (charley horse) are a 'mini' convulsion in the muscle caused by deficiencies of calcium, magnesium, potassium, selenium and/or vitamin E. They range from a subtle eyelid twitch or muscle flutter (fasciculations) in the arms or legs to hard cramps of the feet, calves, back and neck. Prevention is the baseline nutritional supplement program; do a pulse test for food allergies that can cause celiac-type changes and malabsorption, and a hair analysis to check mineral status. Treatment can include liquid colloidal calcium, magnesium and potassium, plus betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day before meals.
claims.verbatim:
MUSCLE CRAMPS (Charley horse): are a
"mini" convulsion that is taking place in the
muscle as a result of deficiencies of calcium,
magnesium, potassium, selenium and/or vitamin E

Wallach's treatment is the over-the-counter decongestant Contac (one capsule every 12 hours) plus the herbs cayenne pepper (Capsicum minimum), eucalyptus (Eucalyptus globulus), German chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla) and scotch pine (Pinus sylvestris).

claims.claim_text: Nausea can be caused by a wide range of diseases and syndromes — from nutritional deficiencies, pregnancy and hepatitis to food allergies and cancer — so Wallach advises that recurring nausea warrants a detailed investigation. For symptom relief he suggests the over-the-counter remedies Pepto-Bismol and Kaopectate, plus the herbs artichoke (Cynara scolymus), avens (Geum urbanum) and peppermint (Mentha piperita).
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of nausea can include Pepto Bismol
Kaopectate, and herbs to include artichoke
(Cynara scolymus), avens (Geum urbanum)
and peppermint (Mentha piperita).

claims.claim_text: Nervous heart (a rapid beat or palpitations when nervous) tends to be common in senior citizens. Wallach says many of these cardiac symptoms result from vitamin B-1 (thiamine, the beri-beri vitamin) deficiency, anemia and a deficiency of stomach acid; do a pulse test to check whether food allergies contribute. His treatment is vitamin B-1 at 100 milligrams three times a day, iron at 45-100 milligrams, an improved general diet and the baseline nutritional supplement program, plus the herbs hawthorn (Crataegus oxyacantha), hops (Humulus lupulus), lavender (Lavandula angustifolia), motherwort (Leonurus cardiaca) and valerian (Valeriana officinalis); avoid offending food allergens and use rotation diets.
claims.verbatim:
NERVOUS HEART (rapid beat or palpitations when nervous): tends to be common
in senior citizens. Many of these cardiac
symptoms are the result of B-l (Beri-Beri)
deficiencies, anemia and deficiencies of stomach acid

claims.claim_text: Nervous tension (nervous headaches) is usually brought on by tension and overwork, and a food allergy may be a trigger, so do a pulse test. Wallach's treatment is to avoid sugar, caffeine and food allergens and to reduce stress and tension, along with exercise, homeopathy, acupuncture, color therapy and subliminal relaxation tapes, plus the herbs balm (Melissa officinalis), bitter orange (Citrus aurantium), sweet woodruff (Galium odoratum), wild celery (Apium graveolens) and lily-of-the-valley (Convallaria majalis).

overwork; there may be a precipitating food

test.

claims.claim_text: Neuralgia (which includes Bell's palsy and neuropathy) is an irritation of a nerve that can stem from many causes — trauma; nutritional deficiencies (vitamin B-12, folic acid, vitamin B-1, vitamin B-6); infections (herpes, shingles); alcoholism; diabetes; and multiple sclerosis. Treatment requires addressing every underlying condition and should also include a B-complex at 50 milligrams three times a day, vitamin B-12 at 1,000 micrograms a day, essential fatty acids as EPA at 5 grams three times a day and flaxseed oil at one tablespoon twice a day, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 and 1,000 milligrams a day, and — for viral neuralgias such as herpes and shingles — the antivirals Isoprinosine at 500-1,500 milligrams a day and Ribavirin at 250-1,500 milligrams a day, plus acupuncture and the herbs lavender (Lavandula angustifolia), oats (Avena sativa), rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis), St. John's wort (Hypericum perforatum) and white willow (Salix alba).
claims.verbatim:
NEURALGIA (Bell's palsy, neuropathy): is
an irritation of a nerve which can be caused by
many diseases ranging from trauma, nutritional
deficiencies (i.e., B-12, folic acid, B-l, B-6,
etc.), infections (i.e., herpes, shingles, etc.),
alcoholism, diabetes, MS, etc.

claims.claim_text: Night blindness (xerophthalmia) is caused by vitamin A deficiency — whether from an outright dietary lack, fat malabsorption (vitamin A is fat-soluble), or zinc deficiency, which impairs the liver's conversion of carotene to vitamin A. Cystic fibrosis, celiac disease and food allergies cause intestinal changes that block absorption of the fat-soluble vitamins (A, E, D and K) and essential fatty acids. The symptom is delayed or complete failure of adaptation to darkness. Wallach's treatment is specific: 25,000-300,000 IU of vitamin A per day as beta carotene and zinc at 15-50 milligrams three times a day.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of night blindness is very specific
with 25,000-300,000 IU of vitamin A per day as
beta carotene and zinc at 15-50 mg t.i.d.

claims.claim_text: Night terrors (nightmares) are almost always caused by food allergies and hypoglycemia. Wallach uses the pulse test and a six-hour glucose tolerance test to find the cause, noting blood sugar bottoms out about 4 to 4.5 hours after eating (especially sugary foods), so night terrors tend to strike roughly four hours after a bedtime snack such as cookies and milk. Bedwetting in children often accompanies night terrors and likewise stems from food allergies (usually milk) and hypoglycemia. Treatment: avoid offending food allergens and sugar, chromium at 25-200 micrograms three times a day, a high-animal-protein diet, the baseline nutritional supplement program, and avoid caffeine.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of night terrors includes avoidance
of offending food allergens, avoidance ofsugar,
chromium at 25-200 mcg t.i.d., high animal
protein diets, base line nutritional supplement
program, avoid caffeine.

claims.claim_text: Nosebleeds (epistaxis) are usually the result of vitamin K and/or vitamin C deficiency; Wallach notes orthodox ear-nose-throat doctors tend to cauterize (burn) the capillaries in the nasal membranes. His treatment: eat more green leafy vegetables; reseed the colon with Lactobacillus acidophilus (the bacteria synthesize vitamin K); vitamin C to bowel tolerance; calcium and magnesium at 2,000 and 1,000 milligrams a day; vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU a day; alfalfa tablets at 5 three times a day with meals; and the herb toad flax (Linaria vulgaris).
claims.verbatim:
Treatment for nosebleeds should include increased consu mption ofgreen leafy vegetables,
reseed colon with Lactobacillus acidophilus
(the bacteria will synthesize vitamin K), vitamin C to bowel tolerance, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day,
vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU per day, alfalfa
tablets at 5 t.i.d. with meals

claims.claim_text: Numbness and tingling in both hands (carpal tunnel syndrome) can be caused by neuralgia (diabetes, vitamin B-12 deficiency), circulation problems and the carpal tunnel itself; food allergies can also cause it, and multiple sclerosis should be considered. Tinel's sign (tapping the wrist to elicit pain) is a clue, and orthodox neurologists favor carpal tunnel surgery. Wallach's treatment is aggressive diagnosis and treatment of any underlying condition plus vitamin B-12 at 1,000 micrograms a day, vitamin B-6 at 200-300 milligrams three times a day, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 and 1,000 milligrams a day, zinc at 50 milligrams three times a day, and colloidal minerals.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment for numbness and tingling should
include aggressive diagnosis and treatment of
any underlying condition as well as B-12 at
1000 mcg per day, B-6 at 200-300 mg t.i.d.,
calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and
1 ,000 mg per day and zinc at 50 mg t.i.d.

claims.claim_text: Obesity (overweight) is, at its simplest, consuming and storing more calories than you use — but Wallach stresses it is not simple. Starvation backfires (the body conserves energy), so eat at least 1,000 calories a day for gradual, permanent loss, with moderate exercise (walking, tennis, golf, swimming, low-impact aerobics). He says 90 percent of obese people overeat and binge because empty-calorie diets trigger 'pica' — a nibbling driven by the body's search for trace minerals — so use colloidal minerals. Test for food allergies (pulse test) and do a six-hour glucose tolerance test for hypoglycemia or diabetes. His program: avoid food allergens, sugar (solid and liquid), caffeine and carbonated drinks (phosphates promote osteoporosis); drink filtered spring water, 8-10 glasses a day; use potassium salt with kelp; don't skip meals (large breakfast, moderate lunch with animal protein, light soup-and-salad dinner); salmon oil at 5 grams three times a day, flaxseed oil one tablespoon twice a day, two tablespoons of nutritional fiber before bed, glucomannan at 1 gram before meals, betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day before meals, and thyroid starting at 1-3 grains (adjust to avoid jitteriness; needing over six grains suggests celiac-type malabsorption). Herbal laxatives or diuretic teas and subliminal weight-loss tapes can also help.

claims.claim_text: Obstruction of the airways (choking) is heralded by the 'universal choking sign' — both hands clutched at the throat and loss of speech; it happens often in restaurants (a 'restaurant coronary' mistaken for a heart attack). Prevention: don't talk while chewing and swallowing, especially meat and firm raw vegetables. Treatment: (1) put a finger into the back of the throat and manually remove the obstruction; (2) perform a Heimlich maneuver (stand behind the patient, lock your arms around them with hands just below the xiphoid cartilage and thrust sharply; for babies use hands only). If the obstruction cannot be cleared, Wallach describes an emergency tracheotomy as a last-resort lifesaving measure — a dead-center incision midway between the base of the larynx and the notch where the collarbones meet the breastbone, large enough for the empty barrel of a ballpoint pen to maintain airflow — followed by CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) if the heart has also stopped.

Wallach's treatment: avoid offending food allergens, double the baseline nutritional supplementation for 30-60 days, acupuncture, and herbs including ginseng (Panax ginseng) and herbal combinations such as Zumbani.

claims.claim_text: Omphalocele (umbilical hernia) is a birth defect — a grape- to basketball-sized, peritoneum-lined skin sac at the navel that may contain fat and/or loops of intestine that can be pushed back into the abdomen. Wallach says it is a common birth defect caused by maternal (and therefore fetal) deficiencies of vitamin A and/or zinc. Treatment: surgery is needed if the hernial ring (the defect in the belly wall) is larger than a fingertip; if it is about a fingertip's diameter it can be healed at home without surgery by taping a golf-ball-sized ball of virgin wool firmly over the hernia and, three times a day, removing it, pushing the fat back in with the fingertip and rubbing the ring in a rotary motion for several minutes to irritate it — over weeks to months the defect fills in and heals.

claims.claim_text: Organic brain syndrome is Wallach's umbrella term for a group of nutritionally-driven mental and behavioral disorders — pellagra, alcoholism, dementia, depression, hyperkinesis (hyperactivity), hypoglycemia, diabetes, premenstrual syndrome (PMS), paranoia, schizophrenia, and learning disabilities. He says they are caused by a wide variety of nutritional deficiencies (niacin/vitamin B-3, vitamin B-1, vitamin B-12, folic acid, chromium and others) and toxicities (alcohol, lead poisoning, and mercury poisoning from dental amalgam fillings). Work-up: do a pulse test to see whether food allergies are involved, and a six-hour glucose tolerance test to rule diabetes or hypoglycemia in or out (a single fasting blood-glucose reading misses 99.9 percent of hypoglycemia and 85 percent of diabetes). Treatment takes serious dedication to find and correct the underlying problems, and should include avoiding food allergens, rotation diets, betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day fifteen minutes before meals, niacin (vitamin B-3) at 450 milligrams three times a day as time-release tablets, essential fatty acids as salmon and flaxseed oils three times a day, chromium at 25-200 micrograms three times a day, zinc at 50 milligrams three times a day, plus the baseline nutritional supplement program.

claims.claim_text: Ornithosis (parrot fever, also called psittacosis) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Chlamydia psittaci. It is caught by inhaling contaminated dust from the feathers, cage bedding, or droppings of infected birds — parrots, parakeets, lovebirds, canaries, and pigeons — and produces an 'atypical pneumonia.' Symptoms include fever, chills, weakness, loss of appetite, and a dry cough that becomes productive; early on it can be mistaken for flu, Legionnaires' disease, or Q fever, so exposure to birds (especially sick ones) is the key diagnostic clue, confirmed by a blood test. Treatment is the antibiotic tetracycline by mouth at 250-500 milligrams four times a day for 10-14 days, with the cough controlled by codeine and strict, enforced bed rest — untreated, parrot fever can be fatal.

claims.claim_text: Osteitis fibrosa (nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism), also known as Paget's disease of bone, is a bone disease — more common in men — in which hard bone is lost and replaced by fibrous connective tissue. It often shows up first in the jaw (separating and loosening the teeth), then in the weight-bearing bones of the pelvis, femur, and tibia, with loss of height and a 'dowager's hump' (kyphosis). Mainstream medicine calls the cause unknown, but in animals it comes from a reversed dietary calcium-to-phosphorus ratio together with relatively large amounts of vitamin D. It is diagnosed by x-ray and by elevated blood alkaline phosphatase and parathyroid hormone. Treatment should include a vigorous effort to correct the dietary calcium/phosphorus ratio: reduce or eliminate red meat, avoid phosphate-containing soft drinks and supplements, reduce vitamin D intake and sun exposure (hats, long sleeves), raise calcium and magnesium intake to 2,000 milligrams and 1,000 milligrams per day, take betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day fifteen minutes before meals, and follow the baseline nutritional supplement program.

claims.claim_text: Osteoporosis is a loss of bone that usually develops in older people, more often in women. Wallach is critical of the standard push for estrogen and fluoride — he says those two alone do not solve the problem, and that estrogen may be contraindicated because of its potential to cause breast and uterine cancer. In his experience osteoporosis is easy to prevent and cure with proper supplementation of stomach acid (hydrochloric acid) and calcium. He recommends a pulse test to find any food allergens that could be causing celiac-type changes and malabsorption. Symptoms include bone pain, joint pain, a 'dowager's hump,' and 'spontaneous' fractures; he calls osteoporosis the 12th most frequent cause of death in adults. Treatment should include betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day fifteen minutes before meals, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 milligrams and 1,000 milligrams per day (or more for the first 30 days), and plant-derived colloidal minerals that include calcium, magnesium, and boron.

claims.claim_text: Otitis (earache) is inflammation of the ear — externa affecting the outer eardrum and ear canal, interna affecting the inner eardrum and the eustachian tube. The standard ear-nose-and-throat approach is antibiotic eardrops and oral antibiotics for acute cases and surgically inserted 'tubes' through the eardrum for chronic ones. Wallach says that in reality 95 percent of all earaches are the result of a milk allergy, which can cause severe fever, painful earaches, and even burst eardrums if not corrected — so do a pulse test before the eardrums are pierced and weakened unnecessarily. Treatment should include hydrogen peroxide or mullein eardrops to relieve local inflammation, strict avoidance of cow's milk in all forms, and the baseline nutritional supplement program; aspirin or acetaminophen (Tylenol) may be needed for pain. Antibiotics are justified only when a streptococcal sore throat or an internal ear infection is cultured.

claims.claim_text: Parasites (worms) include roundworms (ascaris, hookworms, pinworms, whipworms), tapeworms, and microscopic single-celled organisms (amoeba, flagellates). Diagnosis is by a microscopic fecal exam for most intestinal parasites, except pinworms, which need a scotch-tape test. Treatment includes garlic (Allium sativum), peach (Prunus persica), and walnut (Juglans nigra); for heavy infestations needing stronger medication, Wallach lists pyrantel pamoate (for roundworms), niclosamide (for tapeworms), and metronidazole (for protozoa).

claims.claim_text: Parkinsonism (shaking palsy) is caused by degeneration of the basal ganglia of the brain; its symptoms are relentlessly progressive and include muscular rigidity, lack of purposeful movement, and a 'pill rolling' tremor of the thumb and index finger. The cause of true Parkinson's disease is unknown, but many things can cause Parkinsonism-like symptoms: certain drugs (phenothiazines, haloperidol, reserpine), carbon-monoxide poisoning, and excessive manganese supplementation. For drug-induced Parkinsonism, treatment should include eliminating the offending drug, then octacosanol at 300 micrograms three times a day, Neuro-Gen, leucine 10 grams a day, L-methionine 5 grams a day, essential fatty acids one tablespoon twice a day, L-tyrosine 100 milligrams a day, DL-phenylalanine 100 milligrams three times a day, vitamin B-1 at 200 milligrams three times a day, vitamin B-6 at 100 milligrams three times a day, betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 milligrams three times a day before meals, and the baseline nutritional supplement program. He warns that the standard L-Dopa and carbidopa aggravate and speed up Parkinson's in a significant number of cases and have no benefit in more than half.

claims.claim_text: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) has a long history in 'orthodox' medicine — the word derives from 'hysteria,' and the historical treatment was hysterectomy (removing the ovaries and uterus 'cured' the cyclical emotional symptoms but caused an abrupt menopause). claims.claim_text: Pregnancy toxemia (eclampsia) is, in Wallach's view, the result of the low-protein, low-salt diets women were put on to limit weight gain in pregnancy. Pre-eclampsia symptoms include sudden weight gain (fluid accumulation from low blood protein), high blood pressure, and albuminuria (protein in the urine); eclampsia adds convulsions and/or coma, and both characteristically occur after the 20th week of pregnancy. Against the orthodox approach (hospitalize, watch for convulsions, then give barbiturates), treatment of pre-eclampsia should include a high-animal-protein meal plan (150 grams or more, versus the RDA — Recommended Dietary Allowance — of 40 grams), not restricting salt, vitamin B-6 at 100 milligrams per day (dropping to 50 milligrams at birth if you plan to breast-feed, since high B-6 levels reduce breast-milk production), the baseline nutritional supplement program, and 10-12 glasses of water and/or juice per day, especially in the warm summer months.

Treatment should include tetracycline by mouth at 250 milligrams every 4 hours (chloramphenicol may be used in small children to avoid the tooth discoloration tetracycline can cause).

The 'orthodox' ear-nose-and-throat doctor will want to do a tonsillectomy — Wallach urges patients to save their tonsils and refuse it. Treatment should include vitamin A at 300,000 IU per day as beta carotene, zinc at 50 milligrams three times a day, vitamin C to bowel tolerance, gargles with herbal washes, and penicillin G or V at 250 milligrams every 6 hours for 12-14 days.

claims.claim_text: Rabbit fever (tularemia) is caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis, contracted by skinning and dressing infected rabbits or ground squirrels (87 percent of cases). It first appears as a local ulceration at the infection site, then goes systemic into a typhoid-like illness with diarrhea and pneumonia, with high fever and recurring chills and drenching sweats; sputum cultures are highly infectious, so labs should be warned. Treatment of tularemia is with streptomycin intramuscularly at 500 milligrams every 12 hours until the temperature drops into the normal range, then tetracycline by mouth at 250 milligrams four times a day for 10-12 days.

orally at 250 mg q.i.d. for 10-12 days.

claims.claim_text: Rabies (hydrophobia) is a highly dangerous viral disease transmitted through the blood, tissue (including transplanted corneas, livers, kidneys, or hearts), urine, or saliva of infected animals or people. Besides bites from rabid bats, foxes, skunks, and unvaccinated dogs, Wallach notes many fatal cases follow tissue transplants, because rabies in humans is a progressive paralytic disease often misdiagnosed as stroke. He also points out the incubation period is about fourteen days, so if a biting pet has been healthy for three weeks or more, rabies is an impossible diagnosis. Treatment should be started quickly if it is to succeed, and includes the well-known 'rabies shots' every day for ten days plus respiratory support in a hospital setting; high-risk research personnel can get preventive vaccination.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of rabies should be instituted quickly if success can be anticipated;
treatment includes the well known "rabies
shots" every day for ten days and respiratory
support in a hospital setting

claims.claim_text: Rachitic rosary is the bead-like swelling at the junction of the ribs and rib cartilage, seen almost exclusively in small children kept indoors without an oral source of vitamin D; it is easily felt on examination. Wallach treats it as a sign of rickets (vitamin D deficiency). Treatment should include oral vitamin D at 400-1,000 IU per day plus the baseline nutritional supplement program including calcium and magnesium; once the abnormal bony changes normalize, drop the vitamin D dose to 250-400 IU per day, and afford daily sun exposure for at least 30 minutes.
claims.verbatim:
RACHITIC ROSARY (rickets): is the "bead
ing" of the junction between the ribs and the
rib cartilage. This is exclusively a malady of
small children who are kept indoors and are
not getting an oral source of vitamin D. The
rachitic "rosary" is easilypalpated.
Treatment of the rachitic "rosary" should include oral vitamin D at 400-1,000 IU per day
and the base line nutritional supplement program including calcium and magnesium. After the abnormal bony changes become normal, the vitamin D dose should be dropped to
250-400 IU per day; afford daily exposure to
sun for at least 30 minutes

claims.claim_text: Radial nerve palsy ('Saturday night palsy') results from compressing the radial nerve against the humerus — classically by draping the arm over the back of a hard-backed chair for an extended period during a drunken stupor or deep sleep — producing a wrist 'drop,' weakness extending the wrist and fingers, and sometimes a loss of sensory function between the first and second fingers. Treatment should include a B-complex 50 three times a day, topical dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), acupuncture, and hydrotherapy.
claims.verbatim:
Radial
nerve palsy is charac-terized by a wrist "drop"
and weak-ness in the ability to extend the wrist
and fingers; sometimes there is a loss of sensory function between the first and second
fingers.
Treatment of radial palsy should include B-complex 50 t.i.d., topical DMSO, acupuncture
and hydrotherapy

claims.claim_text: Raynaud's disease is marked by tingling and numbness in the fingers (and sometimes the nose and tongue) caused by spasms of the small arteries; the orthodox approach is to cut sympathetic nerves and give anesthetics and tranquilizers. Wallach notes food allergies can be the precipitating factor when arteries are the target tissue (do a pulse test), and to rule out thoracic inlet syndrome. Treatment should include calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day, avoiding offending food allergens and caffeine (coffee, tea, soft drinks, chocolate), vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU per day, essential fatty acids at 5 grams three times a day, L-tryptophan at 500 mg three times a day, acupuncture, chiropractic, and circulation-boosting herbs such as cayenne pepper (Capsicum minimum).
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of Raynaud's disease should include calcium and magnesium at2,000 mg per

1,200 IU per day, essential fatty acids at 5 gm

claims.claim_text: Rectal itching can be caused by candidiasis, food allergies, hemorrhoids, crabs, fleas, or pinworms; Wallach advises a pulse test for food allergies, a self/blood/skin test for candidiasis, the Scotch-tape test to identify pinworm eggs, and a mirror to self-examine the anal folds for fleas or hemorrhoids. Treatment can be palliated with a variety of herbal washes (see hemorrhoids), Preparation H, sitz baths with herbal washes and/or hydrogen peroxide, and specific treatments for the underlying parasites.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of rectal itching can be palliated
with a variety of herbal washes (see hemorrhoids), Preparation H, sitz baths with herbal
washes and/or hydrogen peroxide, specific
treatments for parasites

claims.claim_text: Reye's syndrome occurs most often in young teens, usually in fall and winter, and is thought to be caused by consuming aflatoxin (a toxin of the grain mold Aspergillus flavus); it is marked by pneumonitis, nausea and vomiting, a sudden change in mental status to deep depression, amnesia, agitation progressing to coma and convulsions, fixed dilated pupils, and death in 42-80% of cases. Treatment includes barbiturate anesthesia to lower intracranial pressure, intravenous fluids and electrolytes, pulmonary support, exchange transfusions, and dialysis, plus vitamin C intravenously at 5-10 grams per day, B-complex and B-12 intravenously or intramuscularly, and selenium intramuscularly or intravenously at 250-500 mcg per day.
claims.verbatim:
Vitamin C IV at 5-10 gms per day, B-complex
and B-12 IV or IM, selenium IM or IV at 250-
500 mcg per day.

claims.claim_text: Rheumatic fever is caused by a Streptococcus Group A infection (usually starting as a 'strep throat') and is marked by arthritis, skin rash, fever, heart-valve inflammation, and brain signs (chorea); the residual heart-valve damage is the most dangerous consequence of untreated disease, and diagnosis rests on the typical symptoms plus positive Group A Streptococcus cultures. Treatment early in the course prevents the heart damage and should include aspirin for joint pain and sulfadiazine orally at 500-1,000 mg per day for 1-2 years, or penicillin G or V orally at 250,000 units twice a day for two years.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of rheumatic fever early in the
course of the disease will prevent the heart
damage. Treatment should include aspirin for
joint pain and sulfadiazine orally at 500-1,000
mg/day for 1 -2 years or penicillin G or V orally
at 250,000 u. b.i.d. for two years.

claims.claim_text: Wallach holds that rheumatoid arthritis is not primarily an immune-system disease but is initially caused by infection with a Mycoplasma (PPLO, a pleuropneumonia-like organism) that causes an upper-respiratory infection and then attacks the joint membranes of the fingers and toes, and later the larger joints — a cause he says has been recognized and eliminated in veterinary medicine. Orthodox treatment (aspirin, gold shots, steroids) only relieves symptoms, though he notes 75% of patients improve in the first year with no treatment at all. Treatment should include specific treatment for Mycoplasma/PPLO (Tylosin, tetracyclines, etc.) for six months to one year, intravenous and/or oral hydrogen peroxide, chelation, acupuncture, enterically coated bromelain at 40 mg four times a day, autoimmune urine therapy, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), L-histidine at 1,000 mg three times a day, essential fatty acids at 5 grams three times a day, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day, selenium at 500-1,000 mcg per day, copper at 2-4 mg per day, B-6 at 100 mg three times a day, cartilage at 5 grams three times a day, hydrotherapy, and herbs (topical camphor, black mustard, dandelion, devil's claw, juniper, stinging nettle, sweet vernal grass), plus plant-derived colloidal minerals.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of rheumatoid arthritis should include specific treatment for Mycoplasma
(PPLO) (i.e., Tylosin, tetracyclines, etc.), for
six months to one year, IV and/or oral hydrogen peroxide, chelation, acupuncture,
enterically coated bromeliad at 40 mg q.i.d.,

procumbens), juniper (Juniperus communis),
stinging nettle (Urtica dioica) and sweat vernal
grass (Anthoxanthum odoratum). Plant de-
rived colloidal minerals have proved great
benifit here.

claims.claim_text: Rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D and is marked by stunted growth, joint pain, and deformed long bones (bow legs, dropped wrists, 'sickle shins,' barrel chest, rachitic rosary). Treatment includes supplementation with vitamin D at 400 IU orally, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day, and exposure to sunshine for 30 minutes per day; advanced cases will require orthotic correction and, in some cases, orthopedic surgery.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of rickets includes supple-mentation
with vitamin D at 400 IU orally, calcium and
magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1 ,000 mg per day,
and exposure to sunshine for 30 minutes per
day.

claims.claim_text: Ringworm is caused by fungi (most often Microsporum/Tinea capitis or Trichophyton/Tinea cruris, 'jock itch') that invade the skin, nails, and hair, producing the characteristic circular lesions; cats, rabbits, and children are the most common sources, and diagnosis is by the typical lesions, fungal culture, and a positive Wood's lamp test (Microsporum lesions fluoresce a bright pastel green). Treatment should include Griseofulvin orally at 250 mg four times a day for four months, vitamin A at 25,000-300,000 IU per day as beta carotene, zinc at 50 mg three times a day, vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU per day, ultraviolet light directly to the lesion for up to six minutes per day, and topical herbs including plantain (Plantago major) and castor oil (Ricinus communis).
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of ringworm should include
Griseofulvin orally at 250 mg q.i.d. for four
months, vitamin A at 25,000-300,000 IU/day as
beta carotene, zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., vitamin E at
800-1,200 IU/day, ultra violet light directly to
lesion for up to six minutes per day, and herbs
topically including plantain (Plantgo major)
and castor oil (Ricinus communis).

claims.claim_text: Rocky Mountain spotted fever (tick fever) is caused by a rickettsia (Rickettsia rickettsii) transmitted by the bite of an infected tick (wood, dog, or lone-star tick); it occurs May through October during tick season, mostly along the Eastern seaboard, and affects small children with access to wooded areas (often via the family dog). Symptoms follow 7-12 days after a bite — headaches, chills, weakness, muscle pain, fever, dry cough, and a skin rash starting on the wrists, ankles, palms, soles, and forearms then spreading. Wallach warns: do NOT wait for a positive blood test before starting treatment, as death may occur as quickly as 4-10 days after symptoms appear. Treatment should include tetracycline at 500 mg four times a day orally, or intravenously if the patient cannot swallow capsules, plus supportive intravenous fluids and electrolytes.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of RMSF should include tetracycline at 500 mg q.i.d. orally or IV if the patient
can't swallow capsules. Supportive treatment
with rv fluids and electrolytes is essential to
rapid and full recovery

claims.claim_text: Roseola is an acute viral disease of infants and toddlers marked by high fever (up to 105 F) and a rash that predominates on the belly and chest and lightly on the face and limbs; convulsions may occur during the high-fever periods, and after 3-4 days the child feels completely well even though the rash persists. Treatment is directed to reducing the fever sufficiently to prevent convulsions, plus topical poultices on the rash (see measles).
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of roseola is directed to reducing
the fever sufficiently to prevent convulsions
and topical poultices on the rash (see measles).

claims.claim_text: Scabies ('itch') is caused by an almost microscopic mite (Sarcoptes scabiei) that burrows into the skin; it is very contagious person-to-person, and the original infestation usually comes from an infected animal or contaminated animal bedding. Treatment includes total-body application of 1% gamma benzene hexachloride (lindane) or 25% benzyl benzoate cream in adults, and 5-10% sulfur ointment in infants to avoid potential neurotoxicity; poke (Phytolacca decandra) may be used topically as a natural alternative.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of scabies includes total body application of 1% gamma benzene hexachloride, 25% benzyl benzoate cream in adults and
5-10% sulfur ointment in infants to avoid potential neurotoxicity; poke (Phytolacca
decandra) may be used topically as a natural
alternative

claims.claim_text: Scarlatina (scarlet fever) is caused by a Streptococcus Group A throat infection; the organism releases a toxin that produces a rash most common on the belly, sides, and skin folds, plus a red pulpy 'strawberry' tongue, with fever common in the early stages. Aggressive treatment is recommended to prevent death or rheumatic fever, and diagnosis rests on the characteristic lesions plus positive Group A Streptococcus throat cultures. Treatment of scarlatina is oral penicillin V at 250 mg four times a day for 10-14 days.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of scarlatina is oral peni-cillin V at
250 mg q.i.d. for 10-14 days.

claims.claim_text: Sciatica (low back pain radiating down the buttocks and legs) can be caused by subluxations of the lumbar vertebrae, thinning of a lumbar intervertebral disc, or even a thick wallet in one back pocket; in its most severe form it may result from a ruptured intervertebral disc. Treatment should include hydrotherapy, chiropractic, acupuncture, inversion-gravity therapy, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day, and the baseline nutritional supplement program including plant-derived colloidal minerals.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of sciatica should include hydrotherapy, chiropractic, acupuncture, inversion-gravity therapy, calcium and magnesium at
2,000 mg per day and 1, 000 mg per day and the
baseline nutritional supplement program to
include plant derived colloidal minerals

claims.claim_text: Scoliosis (curvature of the spine) occurs in preteens and teens (80% in girls) during rapid growth; it may be benign or herald early muscular dystrophy, and Wallach attributes it to one set of spinal muscles being stronger than the other from muscle degeneration, with celiac-type intestinal damage and malabsorption as a possible cause. Treatment in the early stages can give a complete cure, while failure to aggressively supplement leads to persistent damage requiring back braces and surgery. Treatment should include avoidance of offending food allergens, vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU per day, selenium at 500-1,000 mcg per day, calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day, and the baseline supplement program including plant-derived colloidal minerals; chiropractic can be very useful for the associated back-muscle spasms.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of scoliosis in the early stages will

claims.claim_text: Scurvy (bleeding gums) is caused by a vitamin C deficiency and may occur concurrently with gingivitis. Treatment should include vitamin C to bowel tolerance, increased intake of green leafy vegetables and fruit, and herbs including dog rose (Rosa canina).
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of scurvy should include vitamin C
to bowel tolerance, increase green leafy vegetables and fruit intake, and herbs including
dog rose (Rosa canina

claims.claim_text: A sebaceous cyst (wen, steatoma) is a slow-growing benign cystic skin 'tumor' containing sebaceous material, frequently found on the scalp (wen), ears, back, or scrotum; it ranges from pea- to golf-ball-sized, is firm (like a soft-shell egg), and painless. Treatment includes a 'stab' incision at the lowest edge of the cyst, evacuating the contents, and flushing with hydrogen peroxide; large cysts require removal of the cyst wall to prevent refilling, placing a sterile gauze drain in the empty cyst and gradually removing it over 7-10 days.
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of a sebaceous cyst includes a
"stab" incision at the lowest edge of the cyst;
evacuate the contents; flush with hydrogen
peroxide.

claims.claim_text: Seborrheic dermatitis (dandruff) is a scaling dermatitis of the scalp and face with normal sebum composition and amount; celiac-type intestinal lesions can be the underlying cause of a malabsorption syndrome. Treatment should include biotin at 100 mcg three times a day, folic acid at 15-25 mg per day, B-6 at 100 mg three times a day, vitamin E at 800-1,200 IU per day, essential fatty acids at 5 grams three times a day, vitamin A at 300,000 IU per day as beta carotene, zinc at 50 mg three times a day, and Selsun Blue shampoo topically.
claims.verbatim:

claims.claim_text: Shark skin (keratosis) is caused by a deficiency of vitamin A and zinc (usually from low-animal-protein diets) and is marked by cracks at the corners of the mouth (cheilosis), oral lesions often secondarily infected by Candida albicans (perleche), 'geographic' tongue, and hard granular plugs in the hair follicles that give a sandpaper-like surface. Treatment of shark skin and related skin problems should include B-complex at 50 mg three times a day, skin washes for dermatitis, vitamin A at 300,000 IU per day as beta carotene, zinc at 50 mg three times a day, and essential fatty acids at 5 grams three times a day.

acids at 5 gm t.i.d

claims.claim_text: Shingles (herpes zoster) is a chronic viral infection with the chicken pox virus, with symptoms including a very painful skin lesion. Treatment should include Isoprinosin at 500-1,500 mg per day, Dermese at 1 four times a day, and American sarsaparilla (Aralia nudicaulis) as a wash or poultice.

Lsoprinosin at 500-1,500 mg per day and
Dermese at 1 q.i.d. and American sarsaparilla

claims.claim_text: Skin ailments (dermatitis) are caused by a variety of diseases. claims.claim_text: Sore throat can be caused by a variety of viral and bacterial diseases; bacterial diseases (such as Streptococcus Group A) tend to produce a higher fever than sore throats caused by viral disease (such as upper respiratory infection, cold viruses, or flu). Treatment of sore throats should include antibiotics as necessary for chronic Strep throat

claims.claim_text: A sprain is a painful stretching of the ligaments of the joints, caused by lifting, sudden stops or turns, or trauma; these injuries can be temporarily debilitating and locally painful. Treatment should include ice to reduce swelling as immediate first aid, wrapping with an Ace bandage for support (fingers may be taped to the adjoining fingers for added support), cartilage at 5 grams three times a day, betaine hydrochloride (betaine HCl) and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 mg three times a day between meals, topical dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and pain gels, and herbs including arnica (Arnica montana) and comfrey (Symphytum officinale).
claims.verbatim:
Treatment of sprains include ice to reduce
swelling as immediate first aid, wrap with an
Ace bandage for support; fingers may be

and pancreatic enzymes at 75-200 mg t.i.d. in
between meals; DMSO topically, pain gels
topically, and herbs including arnica (Arnica
